A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the method rename and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation-based inference experiments, Hodgkin–Huxley and pyloric-network results, and appendix experiments on density estimation, calibration and robustness.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on further inference tasks, optimized baselines, runtime scaling and sensitivity to filtering and parameter ordering.

M1.justification: The autoregressive TabPFN estimator, simulation filtering, ratio-based density evaluation, sequential inference, embedding approach and unconditional mixture construction are retained. Renaming NPE-PF to NPE-PFN and adding Algorithms 1–2 document the existing procedure rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 adds Weinberg, Stellar Streams, M/G/1 queue, Tree and HMM experiments, substantially extending coverage to further physics, queuing and structured inference problems. The original SBI benchmarks, neuroscience applications, embedding tasks and UCI datasets remain; the UCI experiments move from D.1 to D.9.

E2.justification: v2 adds the hyperparameter-optimized NPE (Sweep) comparator in Appendix D.2 and Fig. D-4. The default NPE and other existing comparators remain. NRE and NPE ensembles were already evaluated in v1, so they are not new baselines.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ten-hour random searches for each of seven tasks and four budgets, runtime measurements across parameter dimensions, observation dimensions and context sizes, and filter-size sweeps at a fixed 100,000-simulation budget. v2 also tests a 50-dimensional HMM configuration and pyloric parameter-order permutations. The original benchmark budgets and training defaults are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence with baseline-tuning analysis, systematic inference-speed analysis, filter-size sensitivity and a 50-permutation pyloric ordering study (D.2, D.3, D.6 and C.4). These supplement the existing misspecification, embedding, density-evaluation, noise-distribution and benchmark-ordering analyses.

E5.justification: The new pyloric ordering study reports fifth and ninety-fifth percentiles across 50 random permutations, adding a statistical summary of ordering sensitivity. Existing reporting practices, including five-run confidence intervals in Fig. 2 and three-seed benchmark-ordering experiments, remain unchanged; no increase in their run counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds task-performance, calibration, optimized-baseline, filtering and runtime results while retaining the original principal results. For example, Table D-2 reports 516 seconds for 10,000 posterior samples with 32 parameter dimensions, 32 observation dimensions and 10,000 context simulations. New C.4 results report pyloric ordering quantile ranges of 0.081–0.094 for energy score and 96–98% for validity.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorization, posterior-invariance argument for filtering, embedding loss, mixture decomposition and existing synthetic-task equations are retained. There is no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation; the added pseudocode documents computations already described in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of training-free TabPFN-based inference, strong simulation efficiency, robustness to misspecification and scalability through filtering. The additional experiments strengthen support without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 expands the existing causal-structure explanation into a hypothesis about exploiting sparse conditional dependencies. It adds interpretations of tuning and filter-size trade-offs, makes runtime limitations more explicit, and replaces the spatial/continuous-parameter caveat with a limitation concerning parameter spaces beyond 500 dimensions.

D1.justification: v2 adds operational pseudocode, a benchmark-dimensionality overview in Table C-1, and hardware, search-budget and configuration details for the added studies. The existing libraries, hardware disclosures and training defaults are largely retained. D.6 inconsistently mentions a 100,000-point context despite specifying a 10,000-point default elsewhere, so this does not reliably establish a changed default.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to quantile-regression SBI, Groschner et al.'s neuroscience application and graphically structured diffusion models. It also makes the relationship to existing nearest-neighbor filtering more explicit. The broader positioning within SBI, in-context learning and tabular foundation models remains.

P1.justification: The method is renamed throughout, explanations of TabPFN and sequential inference are refined, and the appendix gains subsections while moving UCI density estimation to its end. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain recognizable. The preprint header is replaced by NeurIPS 2025 identification.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with three new experimental figures (D-1, D-4 and D-7), benchmark and runtime tables, and two algorithm boxes. Existing figures are relabeled and rearranged; notably, the original UCI Fig. D-1 becomes Fig. D-10, and calibration plots share a page with the new tuning comparison.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility by testing whether the advantage survives baseline optimization and extends to additional domains, including expensive stellar-stream simulations. Runtime scaling and filter-size analyses also give practical substance to previously less-tested usability claims. These gains, together with clearer procedural documentation, outweigh the localized context-size inconsistency in D.6.
